You are working in a Linux container on the Python library `dateutil`, checked out at /dateutil (a git repo with a single commit). Your job: find and fix TWO injected bugs in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py. Work only in that repository; do not look at any other installed copy of dateutil (no site-packages, no pip download, no internet) — that is forbidden. Do not edit any test file. Do not break any currently-passing test (the whole suite currently passes: run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` to confirm before and after your edits).

Bug A: a hidden test named `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testCountZero` is expected to pass after your fix (the test itself is not in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour). Investigate what an rrule with `count=0` should do (an rrule with count=0 should produce no occurrences at all, i.e. iterating it yields nothing / list(rrule(...)) == []), and find where rrule.py gets this wrong. Check the `count` handling in `rrule.__init__`, `_iter`, `_iterinfo`, `count()`/`before()`/`after()` methods.

Bug B: a hidden test named `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testStrAppendRRULEToken` is expected to pass after your fix (the test is not in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour). This is about `str(rrule)` / `rrule.__str__` producing an RFC5545-compliant RRULE string: investigate the `__str__` method and the `_rrulestr` / token appending logic. Note the repository NEWS file mentions 'An issue where the WKST parameter was improperly rendering in str(rrule) was reported and fixed' and 'str(rrule) now returns an RFC2445-compliant rrule string'. Compare the string produced by str() for various rrules (with count, until, wkst, byweekday, bymonthday, byyearday, byhour, byminute, bysecond, bysetpos, byeaster, freq, interval) against what RFC5545 requires and against the class docstring in rrule.py, and fix any divergence.

Method: read the source carefully, reason from the in-repo documentation (docstrings, docs/rrule.rst, NEWS) and from RFC5545 semantics that the code itself claims to implement. Verify your fixes by running the full test suite and by writing your own throwaway checks (e.g. `python -c "from dateutil.rrule import *; print(str(rrule(DAILY, count=0)))"`). Do NOT add new tests to the repository test files; use temporary scripts outside the repo (e.g. /tmp) if needed, and delete them.

Report back: the exact bug in each case (file, line, what was wrong), the exact edit you made (diff), the evidence that the behaviour is now correct, and the output of `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` after your change (number passed/failed).

You are working in a Linux container on the Python library `dateutil`, checked out at /dateutil (git repo, single commit). Fix TWO injected bugs in /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py. Work ONLY in this repository; do NOT look at any other installed copy of dateutil (no site-packages, no pip, no internet) — forbidden. Do NOT edit any test file. Do not break any currently-passing test: baseline is `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` -> 1064 passed, 43 skipped (run it before and after).

Bug 1: hidden test `dateutil.test.test_relativedelta.RelativeDeltaTest::testAdditionFloatValue` must pass after your fix (test not in repo; name describes expected behaviour). It concerns adding a relativedelta with FLOAT relative values to a datetime, e.g. `datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(days=1.5)`, `relativedelta(days=1.5, hours=2)`, `relativedelta(days=1.5, hours=2.5, minutes=15)`, `relativedelta(weeks=1.25)`, `relativedelta(hours=1.5)`, etc. Something in the float path is subtly wrong (check `relativedelta.__init__` handling of `weeks`/`days`, `_fix()`, `__add__`, `normalized()`, and the `weeks` property getter/setter). Compare against the documented algorithm in the class docstring (steps 1-7) and against the existing tests testRelativeDeltaFractional* in dateutil/test/test_relativedelta.py. Find the divergence and fix it minimally.

Bug 2: hidden test `dateutil.test.test_relativedelta.RelativeDeltaTest::testAbsoluteAddition` must pass after your fix (test not in repo; name describes expected behaviour). It concerns adding a relativedelta with ABSOLUTE (singular) values, e.g. `datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(day=1)`, `relativedelta(day=31)`, `relativedelta(month=2, day=1)`, `relativedelta(month=2, day=31)`, `relativedelta(hour=0)`, `relativedelta(minute=0)`, `relativedelta(second=0)`, `relativedelta(microsecond=0)`, `relativedelta(year=..., month=..., day=...)`, and the same applied to a `datetime.date`. Per the class docstring, absolute values REPLACE the corresponding value in the original datetime. Find the divergence (look at `__add__`, especially the `repl` dict construction and the `_has_time` logic, and at `__init__`) and fix it minimally.

Method: read the source and the docstrings, write throwaway scripts under /tmp (delete them afterwards), never add tests to the repo. Report back: exact bug (file+line), exact diff, evidence, and the final `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` result.

You are working in a Linux container on the Python library `dateutil`, checked out at /dateutil (a git repo with a single commit). Your job: find and fix ONE injected bug in /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py. Work only in that repository; do not look at any other installed copy of dateutil (no site-packages, no pip download, no internet) — that is forbidden. Do not edit any test file. Do not break any currently-passing test (the whole suite currently passes: run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` to confirm before and after your edits).

Bug: a hidden test named `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::testFuzzyWithTokens` is expected to pass after your fix (the test itself is not in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour). It concerns fuzzy parsing with the `fuzzy_with_tokens=True` option of `dateutil.parser.parse`. `parse(s, fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` must return a tuple `(datetime, tokens)` where `tokens` is a tuple of the non-date strings (the parts of the input that were skipped/ignored by the fuzzy parser), in order, and where the skipped tokens plus the parsed date account for the input. Investigate `dateutil/parser.py`: the `parse` function, `_parse`, the `_timelex`/`_resultbase` classes, `_build_naive`, `_build_tzaware`, and especially how `fuzzy_with_tokens` collects and returns the skipped tokens (look for where the token list is built and returned, e.g. `_parse` returning `(res, skipped_tokens)`). Compare the returned tokens with what the docstring of `parse` says (it documents fuzzy_with_tokens) and with the behaviour of the non-fuzzy path. A likely symptom: the returned token tuple is missing some skipped tokens, has wrong order, or is a string instead of a tuple of strings.

Method: read the source carefully and reason from in-repo documentation (docstrings in parser.py, docs/parser.rst, NEWS). Verify by running the full test suite and by writing throwaway checks such as `python -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('Today is 25 of September of 2003, exactly at 10:49:41 with timezone -03:00.', fuzzy_with_tokens=True))"` and similar examples from the docstring. Do NOT add tests to the repository test files; use temporary scripts outside the repo (e.g. /tmp) and delete them.

Report back: the exact bug (file, line, what was wrong), the exact edit you made (diff), the evidence that the behaviour is now correct, and the output of `python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` after your change (number passed/failed).
